body:
MEASURED against the live store on 2026-08-17. This was the LOAD-BEARING defect of the connector
arc: dynamic registration went from 401 to 201 the moment a shim served this document correctly.

TWO FAULTS IN ONE DOCUMENT.

FAULT 1 — THE LOCATION ANSWERS 401. RFC 9728 puts the metadata for a resource whose identifier has a
path at the PATH-INSERTED well-known URI: for `https://host/default/mcp` that is
`https://host/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/default/mcp`. Loam's well-known set is exact-match
on two root paths, so the path-inserted URI is unrouted, falls through to the mount router, and
answers the uniform 401. A client probing the spec's own location for a PUBLIC discovery document is
told to authenticate — and authenticating requires reading that document. Closed loop, no error text.
The trace shows Claude probing exactly that URI and getting 401.

FAULT 2 — THE IDENTIFIER NAMES THE WRONG THING. The document declares `resource: <origin>` (the
store) while the endpoint a client dials is `<origin>/<mount>/mcp`. A client that validates the
identifier against the URL it connected to sees a mismatch. `protectedResourceDocument(publicUrl)` in
oauth.ts returns `resource: issuerFor(publicUrl)`.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, and it wants a design thought before code: a store has ONE authorization server
and potentially MANY mounts, each with its own MCP door. Each door is a distinct protected resource.
So the honest model is one protected-resource document PER MOUNT, at that mount's path-inserted URI,
naming that mount's endpoint as `resource` and the store as its single `authorization_servers` entry.
The `WWW-Authenticate` challenge the MCP door emits should then point at the document for the mount
that refused, not at a store-wide one.

PREFER AN ADDITIVE FIX AND MEASURE THE COST FIRST. `test/server/oauth-discovery.test.ts` is FROZEN
(T133) and pins the discovery documents; the challenge header may be pinned too. Determine before
writing code whether the new per-mount documents can be ADDED with the root document left byte-
identical — in which case nothing frozen moves and this is one PR. If the challenge URL or the root
document must change, it is two PRs: land the authorization pair in scripts/rail-renames.json first,
then the change. Generate the pairs FROM the diff so the two agree by construction, and verify the
gate answers EXEMPT against a synthetic base before pushing.

DO NOT change the unrouted-path fallthrough to 404 — see T176 for why that would reopen the
mount-existence oracle. Route these paths; leave the fallthrough alone.

RAILS:
1. `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<mount>/mcp` answers 200 with `resource` equal to that
   mount's MCP endpoint URL, exactly.
2. Two mounts answer two documents, each naming its own endpoint — no mount can read another's.
3. The MCP door's 401 challenge names the document for the mount that refused, and fetching that URL
   unauthenticated succeeds.
4. THE ORACLE HOLDS: a path-inserted URI for a mount that does not exist answers the same uniform
   refusal an unknown mount answers, so the metadata surface cannot enumerate mounts.
5. END TO END, the rail that would have caught this: a client that reads ONLY the challenge header and
   the document it names can reach registration. Drive it with real requests, no fixture shortcuts.

TIER: repair — it restores §37's stated promise that a connector can discover this store. Self-merges
on green plus P5, except that the authorization PR (if needed) is Myk's by the two-PR rule.

PART OF THE CONNECTOR ARC: one of four before the debugging proxy comes down. See T176, T178, T148.
title: The protected-resource document names the store, and its RFC 9728 location answers 401
